questions.stem: Evaluate the definite integral of e^x from x=0 to x=2.
questions.solution: The integral of e^x is e^x. Evaluate at the limits: (e^2 - e^0) = e^2 - 1.
questions.explanation: This question tests the ability to integrate an exponential function and apply definite integration.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be forgetting to evaluate the integral at both limits, which would result in an incorrect answer.

questions.solution: The antiderivative of e^(ax) is (1/a)e^(ax). So, for 3e^(2x), the antiderivative is (1/2) * 3e^(2x) = 3e^(2x)/2.
questions.explanation: This question tests the ability to find the antiderivative of an exponential function with a constant coefficient.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be forgetting to divide by the coefficient in front of e^(2x), leading to an incorrect answer.

questions.stem: Integrate the function f(x) = 5e^(-x) from x=1 to x=3.
questions.solution: The integral of e^(-x) is -e^(-x). Evaluate at the limits: (-e^(-3) + e^(-1)) = -e^(-3) + 1/e = 4.
questions.explanation: This question tests the ability to integrate an exponential function with a negative exponent and apply definite integration.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be forgetting to change the sign when integrating e^(-x), resulting in an incorrect answer.

questions.stem: Evaluate the definite integral of e^(2x) from x=-1 to x=1.
questions.solution: The integral of e^(2x) is (1/2)e^(2x). Evaluate at the limits: [(1/2)e^(2) - (1/2)e^(-2)] = e^2 - 1/ e^2.
questions.explanation: This question tests the ability to integrate an exponential function with a power other than 1 and apply definite integration.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be forgetting to divide by the exponent when integrating e^(2x), resulting in an incorrect answer.

questions.stem: Integrate the function f(x) = 6e^(2x) from x=0 to x=ln(3).
questions.solution: The integral of e^(ax) is (1/a)e^(ax). For 6e^(2x), the antiderivative is 3e^(2x). Evaluate at the limits: [3e^(2ln(3)) - 3e^(0)] = 9.
